{{nihongo|'''Ōshima Shrine, Okitsushima Shrine'''|大嶋神社奥津嶋神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Ōshima Shrine / Okutsushima Shrine''' (おおしまじんじゃおくつしまじんじゃ / おきつしまじんじゃ, '''Ōshima–Okutsushima Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Kitatsuda-chō, {{ill|Ōmihachiman|Q385461|qid=Q385461}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It consists of '''Ōshima Shrine''' and '''Okutsushima Shrine''', both of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. The former shrine rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Kami}} (Ōshima Shrine)
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okutsushimahime-no-Mikoto}} (Okutsushima Shrine)

=== Shrine crest ===
Tortoiseshell floral diamond

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was enshrined by {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ar|الإمبراطور سيمو|arz|الامبراطور سيمو|azb|سیمو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Seimu|cs|Seimu|de|Seimu|es|Seimu Tennō|fa|امپراتور سیمو|fi|Seimu|fr|Seimu|hr|Seimu|hu|Szeimu japán császár|id|Kaisar Seimu|it|Seimu|ja|成務天皇|ka|სეიმუ|ko|세이무 천황|nl|Seimu|pl|Seimu|pt|Seimu|ru|Император Сэйму|sh|Car Seimu|simple|Emperor Seimu|sl|Cesar Sejmu|sv|Seimu|th|จักรพรรดิเซมุ|tl|Emperador Seimu|tr|Seimu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Сейму|uz|Imperator Seimu|vi|Thiên hoàng Seimu|yo|Emperor Seimu|zh|成務天皇|zh_min_nan|Seimu Thian-hông|zh_yue|成務天皇|qid=Q316672}}. Ōshima Shrine and Okutsushima Shrine were originally enshrined at separate locations, but were relocated to the same site prior to the 6th year of {{ill|Enbun|Q1145071|qid=Q1145071}} ({{ill|1361|Q6159|qid=Q6159}}). Ōshima Shrine is classified as a Shikinaisha minor shrine, while Okutsushima Shrine is a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}. According to the '{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}', in the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), it was granted the divine rank of Junior Fifth Rank Upper Grade.

In the 3rd year of {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} ({{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}}), it was designated as a Prefectural Shrine.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties (national designation) ===
* Seated wooden statue of Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto (Sculpture) – Heian period work. Designated September 2, 1909 (Meiji 42)<ref>{{National Cultural Properties Database|201|3328|Seated Wooden Statue of Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}</ref>.
* Chrysanthemum mother-of-pearl inlaid saddle, black lacquered saddle, black lacquered stirrups (Crafts) – Late Heian to Kamakura period works. Designated June 9, 1981 (Shōwa 56)<ref>{{National Cultural Properties Database|201|7223|{Chrysanthemum Mother-of-Pearl Inlaid Saddle (front ring missing) / Black Lacquered Saddle / Black Lacquered Stirrups}}}</ref>.
* Ōshima and Okutsushima Shrine documents (222 items): 1 scroll, 32 volumes, 3 sheets (Calligraphy) – Documents from the Kamakura to Edo periods. Designated June 6, 1987 (Shōwa 62)<ref>{{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9093|Ōshima and Okutsushima Shrine Documents (222 items)}}</ref>.
